title: Detention and Homecoming
premise: Casper Marchetti has spent seventeen years perfecting the art of being unremarkable, hiding their anxiety in sourdough and their grief over their late grandmother in the family bakery's locked recipe box. When a group chat of five detention regulars starts receiving messages predicting events hours before they happen, Casper realizes the prophecies are tied to the bread they bake — each loaf carries a feeling, and feelings are leaking into the future. To stop the predictions from turning catastrophic, Casper must lead their ragtag team to win the state baking championship (the one nobody cares about) and finally audition for the conservatory they've secretly dreamed of — because the final prophecy shows the bakery burning down unless someone claims what they truly want. In the end, Casper wins neither contest outright but tells the truth about who they are, breaking the loop: the group chat goes silent, the bakery stands, and Casper comes home to a family that finally sees them.
about_author: L. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former pastry line cook who spent three years writing on the night shift between proofing cycles. They live in a small coastal town where they still judge bakeries too harshly and believe every kitchen holds at least one secret worth telling.

chapters.title: The Proofing Hour
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. After landing in detention for a flour-dust fire alarm mishap, Casper bonds with four misfits — Priya, Dez, Marisol, and quiet Theo — who form a group chat as a joke. That night, baking their grandmother's grief-bread recipe, Casper texts a prediction that comes true by morning. The emotional beat: reluctant connection cracking open a carefully sealed loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Yeast Knows
chapters.summary: Rotating POV among the five friends. The chat's predictions grow precise and unsettling — a flooded gym, a teacher's resignation — all traceable to loaves Casper baked with strong emotions. Dez pushes to exploit the gift; Theo warns it's a debt being collected. The beat: wonder curdling into fear as the friends realize Casper's suppressed feelings are the engine.

chapters.title: Championship Conditions
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV anchors the middle act. The final prophecy arrives: the Marchetti Bakery burns unless Casper enters and wins the state championship AND auditions for the Halbrook Conservatory before finals week. Training montage chaos, sabotage from rival baker Ash Wren, and Casper's panic attack mid-competition reveal the truth to their parents. The beat: loyalty strained as the team debates whether winning or honesty saves the bakery.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the championship final, Casper abandons the prophesied showpiece and bakes an honest loaf about wanting to be seen — losing to Ash but breaking the prophecy's grip, since the curse fed on concealment. The audition follows, imperfect and true. The bakery doesn't burn; the group chat sends one last message: 'You're home.' The beat: belonging earned not through victory but through visibility.
